Lorroakan is the human proprietor of Sorcerous Sundries, in Act 3 of Baldur's Gate 3. He is in Ramazith's Tower, after traveling there from Sorcerous Sundries in the Lower City of Baldur's Gate.

He is searching for something called the Nightsong, and offers a large reward for finding it.

“
Witness me - immortal, until the end of all days.
„
— Lorroakan, after imprisoning Dame Aylin

Involvement

Act One

Lorroakan is first mentioned by  Aradin Beno in Act One, whom the party meets outside of the Druid Grove. Aradin tells the party about a huge sum of money offered by a wizard in exchange for retrieving a treasure called the  Nightsong. This starts ⁠Find the Nightsong.

He is also mentioned by  Rolan, who is especially proud that Lorroakan has accepted him as his student; this being his primary reason for travelling to Baldur's Gate.  Gale, however, notes he has heard that Lorroakan is a bit of a cad.

Act Three

Arriving in the city of Baldur's Gate in Act Three, Lorroakan can be met to find out what he wants with the Nightsong.

Manning the till at Sorcerous Sundries, the party can meet Rolan with a bloodied face. A successful Insight check reveals that, despite his cheerful tone, there is something wrong. If he is asked about the Nightsong, Rolan divulges that many people have come to claim Lorroakan's bounty to no avail. He also warns them about Lorroakan's temper if they plan on bringing him information about the Nightsong.

Upon heading upstairs, the party is greeted by  Lorroakan's Projection.

There are four portals, one of which is the correct one to transport the party to him. Using the far left pale blue portal, with the plaque that reads "The Nightsong is an immortal being, the child of a deity", teleports the party to Ramazith's Tower in the Upper City where Lorroakan is using his assistant  Miklaur as target practice for his Animated Armour,  Krank. Noticing the party, he questions them on whereabouts of the Nightsong.

Unbeknownst to the party, Lorroakan has been in contact with  Ketheric Thorm and  Balthazar and has been searching for the Nightsong, who already has been revealed to the party to be Dame Aylin, to grant himself the very same immortality Ketheric had.[1]

The party can answer truthfully as to the whereabouts of Aylin and succeed various Ability Checks to deceive him into believing that she has been killed.

If Aylin is at camp and is later informed of Lorrokan's intentions, she angrily departs for Ramazith's Tower to confront him, despite  Isobel's efforts to stop her.

Alternatively, if Lorroakan is successfully deceived, and Aylin is as well, there is no confrontation.

Helping the Nightsong

If the party side with Aylin, Lorroakan is joined in battle by one of each elemental type of Myrmidon, all able to  Fly at will. The Earth Myrmidon can cast  Stoneskin on him, and each myrmidon unlocks one spell slot for him until defeated. Miklaur and Krank also join the fray against the party.

Lorroakan's death brings an end to the hunt for Aylin. The party gain the following inspiration:

  • ⁠Never To Be Chained Again ( Folk Hero backgrounds)
  • ⁠How High They Fall ( Haunted One backgrounds)
  • ⁠Stopping the Repetition of History ( Sage backgrounds)

If his family was saved during Act Two, Rolan takes over as proprietor of Sorcerous Sundries and promises aid for ⁠Gather Your Allies, granting  Rolan's Firestorm during the final battle. If they were not saved, he fights alongside Lorroakan.

Helping Lorroakan

If the party side with Lorroakan, Aylin becomes hostile, summoning four  Moonlight Silvers to her aid.

If defeated, Lorroakan jails Aylin in another soul cage, finally obtaining his long sought-for immortality. Lorroakan rewards the party with 5000 gold and lends his aid for ⁠Gather Your Allies, granting  Lorroakan's Firestorm during the final battle (an identical Class Action to Rolan's). The inspiration ⁠The Karsus of Our Times is also granted to party members with the Sage background. In the High Hall, Lorroakan appears with the  Invulnerability condition, granting him Immunity to all damage types.

If the party return to Isobel and inform her of Aylin's recapture, but deceive her as to their betrayal, Isobel rushes to Ramazith's Tower to confront Lorroakan herself.

If the party travel there after this, only her corpse is found, having been killed by Lorroakan off-screen. Having witnessed the death of her lover, Aylin reels where she stands, imprisoned and horrified, and vows to murder the player character (and their descendants) upon her escape. Lorroakan himself makes no mention of the fight.

Speak with Dead

Lorroakan can be spoken to through the use of  Speak with Dead.

  • How did you become the owner of this place?
    • Lorroakan
      Ramazith... gone... Open for the taking...
      • Who is Ramazith?
        • Lorroakan
          Powerful mage... spell-maker...
      • Where did Ramazith go?
        • Narrator
          *The corpse remains silent. It does not know.*
  • How did you learn to imprison the Nightsong?
    • Lorroakan
      Ramazith's notes... Balthazar's magic...
  • Who is more powerful, you or your apprentice?
    • Narrator
      *The corpse pauses, perhaps resisting the truth.*
      • Lorroakan
        That... bloody... tiefling...
  • Where do you store your valuables?
    • Lorroakan
      Lower floor... magic repository... vault key...
      • Any security measures I should be aware of in your repository?
        • Lorroakan
          Traps... spells... deathly to the touch...
          • How do I avoid the traps?
            • Lorroakan
              All magic... can be... dispelled...

Notes

  • Lorroakan's myrmidons have weaker weapons compared to other myrmidons encountered throughout the game. They do not have innate elemental damage components and are not enchanted. The unique weapon abilities are not changed.
  • Lorroakan first appeared in the  Murder in Baldur's Gate adventure for the 5th Edition Dungeons & Dragons as well as  Baldur's Gate: Descent into Avernus.
    • In D&D 5e, he is the current owner of Ramazith's Tower in the Upper City while Sorcerous Sundries belonges to another wizard,  Rivalen Blackhand. Lorroakan is broke and has an ever-pressing need for money, and he desperately wants to learn the late wizard Ramazith's secrets of wealth that lie beneath his tower. Lorroakan is eager to hire some adventurers to do it for him.
    • It is possible that, when the Upper City was scrapped early in development, Larian had to move Lorroakan and his storyline to Sorcerous Sundries, making him a wealthy proprietor of both buildings. It is also possible that Sorcerous Vault was initally designed to be Ramazith's Vault as it has tower-like features. The door in the Sorcerous Vault which leads to the Archmage hub is titled "Ramazith".
  • If Gale is brought along to meet Lorroakan while proceeding with his quest The Wizard of Waterdeep, the two will bicker over the artifacts they each desire: the Nightsong and the Crown of Karsus.
  • As of Patch #7, Lorroakan no longer has  Opportunity Attack.
